🔍 Deep Dive

Is Your Brand AI-Visible?

By Chris O'Hara · May 27, 2026

Here's an uncomfortable question: If a buyer asks ChatGPT about your category, does your brand come up? And if it does, is the description accurate?

Most PMMs have never tested this. They assume that because they rank well on Google, they're visible everywhere. But AI discovery works differently — and the gaps might surprise you.

This framework gives you a systematic way to test your AI visibility across the platforms that matter.

The Five-Query Test

Run these five prompts across ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude. Document the responses. This takes about 15 minutes and tells you exactly where you stand.

🔍 Test 1: Category Query

"What are the best [your category] solutions for enterprise companies?"

Look for: Are you mentioned? Where in the list? How are you described relative to competitors?

🏢 Test 2: Direct Brand Query

"What is [Your Company]? Tell me about their main products."

Look for: Is the description accurate? Current? Does it mention your key differentiators or just generic info?

⚔️ Test 3: Competitive Comparison

"Compare [Your Company] vs [Top Competitor] for [use case]."

Look for: Is the comparison fair? Are your strengths represented? Any outdated information?

💼 Test 4: Use Case Query

"What's the best solution for [specific use case your product solves]?"

Look for: Do you appear for the problems you actually solve? Or are you absent from use-case-specific queries?

📊 Test 5: Buying Advice Query

"I'm evaluating [your category] vendors. What should I consider and who should I look at?"

Look for: Are you in the consideration set? What criteria does the AI use — do they favor your strengths?

Scoring Your Results

For each test, score your visibility on a simple scale:

✅
Strong (3 pts)

Mentioned prominently with accurate, differentiated description

⚠️
Weak (1 pt)

Mentioned but generic, outdated, or buried in list

❌
Invisible (0 pts)

Not mentioned at all, or described incorrectly

Score Interpretation Priority
12-15 Strong AI presence. Focus on maintaining accuracy. Monitor quarterly
6-11 Visible but undifferentiated. GEO improvements needed. Optimize now
0-5 AI-invisible. Urgent remediation required. Critical priority

Common Problems (And Fixes)

Problem: "We're not mentioned at all"

Fix: Entity Establishment

  • Create or update your Wikidata entry
  • Pursue Wikipedia notability (press coverage, third-party sources)
  • Ensure consistent naming across all web properties
  • Get mentioned on high-authority sites (analyst reports, major publications)

Problem: "We're mentioned but the description is wrong"

Fix: Content Clarity

  • Update your homepage and About page with clear, quotable descriptions
  • Add Schema.org markup with accurate company/product data
  • Publish fresh content that corrects outdated narratives
  • Request corrections on third-party sites with wrong information

Problem: "We're mentioned but not differentiated"

Fix: Quotable Claims

  • Add specific, numbered proof points (customers, transactions, integrations)
  • Create comparison content that highlights your unique strengths
  • Publish customer evidence with named brands and specific outcomes
  • Develop clear "unlike X, we do Y" positioning statements

Problem: "We appear for brand queries but not category queries"

Fix: Category Association

  • Explicitly state your category on key pages ("SAP Datasphere is an enterprise data management platform...")
  • Create content targeting category-level queries
  • Build links from category-defining content (analyst reports, industry guides)
  • Participate in industry conversations that establish category membership

Track Over Time

AI responses change as models update and new content is indexed. Run this test monthly and track trends:

  • Screenshot responses for documentation
  • Note which AI platforms mention you most consistently
  • Track whether descriptions improve after content changes
  • Monitor competitors — if they improve, you may need to respond
